chunks: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani informed us. He said: Ahmad b. Salih narrated to us from Hakim b. Abd al-Rahman. He said: Muqatil b. Sulayman narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said to Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him): O Ali! You are to me as Habatullah was to Adam, and as Sam was to Nuh, and as Ishaq was to Ibrahim, and as Harun was to Musa, and as Sham'un was to Isa, except that there is no prophet after me. O Ali! You are my deputy and my vicegerent. So whoever denies your deputyship and your vicegerency, he is not from me and I am not from him, and I will be his adversary on the Day of Resurrection. O Ali! You are the best of my nation in virtue, the foremost of them in affability, the most knowledgeable of them, the most forbearing of them, the boldest of them in heart, and the most generous of them with their hands. O Ali! You are the Imam after me and the emir. You are the companion after me and the vizier. You have no equal in my nation. O Ali! You are the divider of Paradise and the Fire. By your love, the righteous will be known from the wicked, and the evil will be distinguished from the elect, and the believers from the disbelievers.
May Allah's blessings be upon His Messenger Muhammad and his family.

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: in the position/station of, a key term establishing Ali's rank relative to previous prophets' successors
key_terms.قَسِيمُ الْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّارِ: the divider of Paradise and the Fire, indicating Ali's role in distinguishing believers from disbelievers
key_terms.وَصِيِّي وَخَلِيفَتِي: my deputy and my vicegerent, the two central titles of succession

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Imam Ali's station compared to previous prophets' successors?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition from Al-Amali of al-Saduq, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) addresses Imam Ali (AS) directly, declaring his exalted status by drawing parallels between Ali's relationship to him and the relationships of chosen successors to previous prophets: Habatullah to Adam, Sam to Nuh, Ishaq to Ibrahim, Harun to Musa, and Sham'un to Isa. The Prophet emphasizes that Ali is his deputy, vicegerent, and the imam after him, and that love for Ali serves as the criterion by which the righteous are distinguished from the wicked on the Day of Judgment.
